what_its_for: Crisaborole is a prescription ointment used to treat mild to moderate eczema (also called atopic dermatitis) in adults and children 3 months of age and older. It helps reduce the redness, itching, and irritation caused by eczema by calming inflammation in the skin.
how_to_take: This medicine is applied directly to your skin. Wash your hands before and after applying the ointment. Apply a thin layer to the affected skin areas twice a day. Gently rub it in. Do NOT apply inside your mouth, eyes, nose, or vagina. Do NOT cover the treated area with tight bandages or wraps unless your doctor tells you to. This medicine is for skin use only — do not swallow it.
dosing: Apply a thin layer to the affected skin areas TWO TIMES A DAY (morning and evening). Use only the amount needed to cover the affected areas. Your doctor will tell you which areas of skin to treat. Do not use more than directed.
missed_dose: If you forget to apply a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do not apply extra ointment to make up for a missed dose.
storage: Store crisaborole ointment at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat and direct sunlight. Keep the tube tightly closed when not in use. Keep this medicine out of reach of children. Do not flush unused medicine down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about proper disposal.
what_to_avoid: Avoid getting the ointment in your eyes, mouth, nose, or other sensitive areas. If accidental contact occurs, rinse the area well with water. Avoid using other skin products on the same area unless your doctor approves. Do not share this medication with others, even if they have similar skin symptoms.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience: burning, stinging, or pain at the application site that is severe or does not go away; signs of an allergic reaction such as hives, rash, swelling of the face, lips, tongue or throat, or difficulty breathing; any new or worsening skin symptoms. Also call your doctor if your eczema does not improve after using this medicine as directed.
when_it_works: You may start to notice some improvement in your eczema symptoms within a few days, but it may take up to 4 weeks to see the full benefit. Keep using the ointment as directed even if your skin starts to feel better. Talk to your doctor if you do not see improvement after 4 weeks of regular use.
special_populations: CHILDREN: Crisaborole is safe to use in children 3 months and older. A parent or caregiver should apply the ointment for young children. Keep the ointment away from a child's hands and mouth. PREGNANCY AND BREASTFEEDING: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. There is limited information about the safety of crisaborole during pregnancy or breastfeeding. If breastfeeding, avoid applying the ointment directly to the breast or nipple area. ELDERLY: No special dosing adjustments are needed for older adults, but always follow your doctor's instructions.
